Definition: from G575 and a derivative of G4632; to pack up (one's) baggage:--take up… carriages.
BiblicalUsage: After the stay at Caesarea, Paul and his company packed up their baggage and went up to Jerusalem. The word is the ordinary business of a journey ending and a harder one beginning.
TheologicalSignificance: Obedience sometimes looks as plain as packing a bag and going where you know trouble is waiting.
